thread.title: Stocks, Dow Jones Slide On Apple, Chips, Retail | Investor's Business Daily

author: ALAN R. ELLIOTT
title: Stocks, Dow Jones Slide On Apple, Chips, Retail | Investor's Business Daily
text:
Stocks veered into deep early losses Tuesday, as leading tech stocks plummeted and the Dow Jones industrial average cut deep below the 25,000 mark.
X Apple ( AAPL ) and the FANG stocks took big early losses, and chip stocks came under significant early pressure. Several big retail names sold off hard following earnings reports, with Target ( TGT ), L Brands ( LB ), Kohl's ( KSS ) and Lowe's ( LOW ) leading those declines.
Boeing ( BA ) and Apple spearheaded the losses on the Dow Jones industrials, which dropped 1.9%. The S&P 500 opened took a 1.7% loss.
The Nasdaq Composite swooned 2%, hurt by Apple, and as chip-sector names took a premarket beating. Micron Technology ( MU ) and Advanced Micro Devices ( AMD ) fell more than 5%. Nvidia ( NVDA ) skidded 4% lower.

Please contact customer service CLOSE Stock Market Digests Trade Fears, Housing Data Mixed Markets continue to gyrate ahead of next week's G20 summit in Argentina, where President Donald Trump and China's Xi Jinping are expected to dive into long-anticipated trade negotiations. Trump stirred optimism on Friday, saying he expected to make a deal during the meeting and that he didn't want to put " China in a bad position ."
That optimism unraveled on Saturday, when Vice President Mike Pence and China's Xi met in Papua New Guinea. The pair reportedly sparred verbally , pointing fingers and laying blame for the economic war underway between the two countries.
Tuesday's early economic news showed a weaker-than-expected 2% jump in October housing starts. The Commerce Department put the annualized pace of new starts at 1.228 million for the month, up from 1.201 million for September, but below analyst views for 1.24 million. Building permits were issued at an annualized rate of 1.263 million, up from September's 1.241 million and just above views for a rate of 1.26 million.
Dow Jones Tests 25,000, Nasdaq Eyes New Low The Dow Jones industrial average undercut its 50-day line of support on Monday, ending the session flush at the 25,000 mark. A slip below that mark would leave the index ready for another, lower test, at the level of its Oct. 29 low. The Nasdaq ended the session 1.5% above its Oct. 29 low. The S&P 500 was in somewhat stronger position, holding 1.8% off its October low. The S&P 500 is 4% below its 50-day moving average. The Nasdaq was 8% below that line of support, and 13.5% off its August peak.
Monday's stock market trading in the U.S. carried over to China's stock markets, sending Hong Kong's Hang Seng index down 2% and the Shanghai Composite to a 2.1% loss. In Japan, Tokyo's Nikkei 225 dropped 1.1%.
Europe's markets swung into deeper losses in afternoon trade. Bank of England Governor Mark Carney soothed markets early, telling lawmakers that British banks were well-prepared for the potential impact from economic shifts likely under the U.K.'s Brexit initiative. London's FTSE 100 traded down 0.8%. Frankfurt's DAX and the CAC-40 in Paris both lost more than 1.3%.
Apple Embraces Bear Status; Campbell, Urban Outfitters Jump Apple stock opened down 3.5%. As of Tuesday, Apple constituted a bit more than 5% of the weight of the Dow Jones industrial average, placing it at sixth on the list. It ranks first among weightings on the Nasdaq 100 list, at slightly more than 11% of the index. Apple shares are now nearing a free-fall, working on their eighth straight down week, well below their 40-week moving average and down more than 20% from a Oct. 3 high. The last time Apple shares fell more than 20% was in April-May of 2016.
Among so-called FANG stocks, Netflix ( NLFX ) and Amazon.com ( AMZN ) led the retreat, down 3.4% and 2.7%, respectively.
There were several bright spots in early trade. Packaged food leader Campbell Soup ( CPB ) surged 6% following its fiscal first-quarter report. Analog DevicesADI countered the chip trend, rising 1.9% on its earnings results. Among retailers, Urban Outfitters ( URBN ) jumped 1.3% after an above-forecast solid third-quarter report.
Best BuyBBY managed a 1% advance, after third-quarter results comfortably cleared estimates. Management projected sames-store-sales growth at zero to 3% for the holiday shopping season. vs. a 4.3% gain in the third quarter.
Big-box retailer Target tanked 9%, after both earnings and revenue missed analysts' projections for the third quarter . The stock ended Monday 13.9% below its mid-September high.
Victoria's Secret owner L Brands careened 12% lower in early trade. Fiscal third-quarter sales and earnings narrowly topped analyst targets, but the company halved its annual dividend to $1.20.
Among other retail names in motion, Kohl's plummeted 9% and Lowe's dropped 3.5% after their quarterly reports. TJX ( TJX ) shed 1.6% and Ross Stores ( ROST ) crumbled 3.3% on the heels of their earnings reports.
